messages:
jorge: Heads-up — hit a cancellation/cleanup quirk with the Go SDK generator streaming API while building a tiny sample. Repro link below.
jorge: Minimal repro:```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
defer cancel()
gen := client.Generator("redwood/gpt-gen")
stream, err := gen.Stream(ctx, &GenRequest{Prompt: "stream me"})
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
for {
  tok, err := stream.Recv()
  if err == io.EOF { break }
  if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
  fmt.Print(tok.Text)
}
```
jorge: Behavior: cancelling ctx after receiving first token does NOT terminate the server-side work; connection goroutines linger and server continues streaming until model finishes. Looks like ctx only governs the initial handshake.
sam: Which SDK version? we patched a similar race a while back but this sounds like the reader isn't watching ctx.Done().
sam: Can you paste the sample app or commit?
jorge: Repo: https://github.com/redwood/inference-samples/go-gen-cancel-repro. Using go-sdk v0.15.2.
priya: I remember the original design favored keeping the stream reader independent to avoid mid-stream protocol races; that might be why ctx isn't wired through. But we should support cooperative cancel. :thinking_face:
jen: Does the stream type expose a way to half-close or abort (CloseSend/Abort)? If not, that's UX friction.
jorge: Current Stream has Recv() and Close() that blocks until EOF; no abort/CloseSend.
jen: That's rough for onboarding examples where users want to stop early.
ci-bot: [CI] PR #2345  generator-stream-cancel-tests  failed 1 test
ci-bot: output snippet: "goroutine leaked: 3 goroutines contain net/http: Transport: request canceled (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)"
alex: Confirmed — stream handshake honors ctx but the read loop does not select on ctx.Done(), so midstream cancel can leave a goroutine stuck on conn.Read.
alex: Quick mitigation: spawn a goroutine that selects on ctx.Done() and closes the underlying transport/net.Conn. Need care for double-close semantics in tests.
priya: Python SDK supports client-side midstream abort by closing the SSE/ws connection; parity gap here.
marta: Should we add an Abort method to the public API or silently wire ctx into the implementation?
sam: Short-term: implement internal wire-up so ctx cancels close the conn. Long-term: add an explicit Abort/CloseSend API for ergonomics.
jen: Also add a short sample in the repo demonstrating context cancellation for streaming generators — helps onboarding and reduces confusion.
alex: I'll open a small PR to watch ctx.Done() and close transport; add unit tests verifying no goroutine leaks and that server observes the cancel. PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/3456
alex: Will add a concise note to the Go SDK README about generator cancellation semantics and include an example snippet.
priya: I'll add a python-go parity test to the e2e suite so we catch regressions.
sam: Filing an issue for explicit Abort API to hash out ergonomics: https://github.com/redwood/inference/issues/789
jorge: Thanks everyone. Once the PR lands I'll update the sample repo and verify behavior. :tada: 
marta: Action items: alex opens PR, priya adds parity test, jen adds sample snippet and README note, sam owns follow-up API issue.
jorge: Appreciate the speedy triage — this was blocking a product demo but now feels tractable.
